title: Tracing Uncertainties of Extreme El Ni\~{n}o Prediction to Mesoscale Ocean Currents
abstract: arXiv:2611.17854v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The predictability of the El Ni\~{n}o-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) has historically been linked to large-scale errors in models' initial conditions such as heat content and surface wind stress. Here we demonstrate that these slowly evolving errors may ultimately originate from mesoscale errors in initial oceanic states that are common in current models and ocean observation systems. This hidden source of ENSO forecast uncertainty, in terms of mesoscale ocean-current errors, is convincingly exposed by the conditional nonlinear optimal perturbation (CNOP) method applied to a differentiable ocean AI model. The CNOP-identified most influential current errors are strongly event-dependent. translated_title: 将极端厄尔尼诺预测的不确定性追溯到中尺度洋流
translated_abstract: 厄尔尼诺-南方振荡（ENSO）的可预报性历来被认为与模式初始条件中的大尺度误差有关，例如热含量和表面风应力的误差。本研究证明，这些缓慢演变的误差可能最终源于初始海洋状态中的中尺度误差，而这类误差在当前的模式和海洋观测系统中普遍存在。这一隐藏的ENSO预报不确定性来源——即中尺度洋流误差——通过将条件非线性最优扰动（CNOP）方法应用于可微分海洋AI模型而得到了令人信服的揭示。CNOP所识别出的最具影响力的洋流误差具有强烈的事件依赖性：对于1997/98年厄尔尼诺事件，东太平洋的初始洋流误差通过局部抑制原有的次表层增暖而造成了最大的预报误差；对于2015/16年事件，主导误差则来自西太平洋……（原摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该研究将条件非线性最优扰动（CNOP）方法应用于可微分海洋AI模型，首次揭示了极端厄尔尼诺预测不确定性可追溯至初始海洋状态中的中尺度洋流误差，且这些误差的来源具有强烈的事件依赖性。
en_tdlr: By applying the conditional nonlinear optimal perturbation (CNOP) method to a differentiable ocean AI model, this study reveals that uncertainties in extreme El Niño prediction can be traced to mesoscale ocean-current errors in initial ocean states, which are strongly event-dependent.
